title: Minimum Edges for Graph Dimension d
description: Studies the function minEdges(d) giving the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension exactly d. Formalizes known values (d=0..5), proves structural results including a constructive simplex embedding of K_n in ℝⁿ, shows the complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity, analyzes growth rates, and introduces the deficiency function.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)

sections.title: Header and Imports
sections.mathContext: Erdős #1007: the graph dimension $\dim(G)$ (least $n$ with a unit-distance embedding in $\mathbb{R}^n$) and the minimum-edge function $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)$.

sections.title: §1. Graph Dimension
sections.mathContext: A unit-distance embedding realizes adjacent vertices at distance 1 in $\mathbb{R}^n$; $\dim(G)$ is the least such $n$.
sections.summary: §1. The notion of a unit-distance embedding `hasUnitEmbedding'` of a graph in $\mathbb{R}^n$, inherited from the parent file.

sections.title: §1b. Simplex Embedding Construction
sections.mathContext: Embed vertex $i$ as $\tfrac1{\sqrt2}e_i\in\mathbb{R}^n$; pairwise distances are all $1$, giving a unit embedding of $K_n$.
sections.summary: §1b. The key simplex embedding $i\mapsto\tfrac1{\sqrt2}e_i$: its squared-distance computation, the resulting unit-distance embedding of $K_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge2$), and inheritance by subgraphs.

sections.title: §1c. Embedding Existence (Proved)
sections.mathContext: Every irreflexive (loop-free) graph admits a unit embedding in some $\mathbb{R}^n$; loops make it impossible.
sections.summary: §1c. Existence: every irreflexive graph admits a unit-distance embedding in some $\mathbb{R}^n$ (via the complete-graph simplex embedding), while self-loops force non-existence.

sections.title: §1d. Graph Dimension Definition
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{graphDimension}'(G)$ = least $n$ admitting a unit embedding, well-defined for irreflexive graphs.
sections.summary: §1d. The definition of `graphDimension'` as the least dimension admitting a unit-distance embedding, using the existence result of §1c.

sections.title: §2. Minimum Edge Function
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)$ = fewest edges in a graph of dimension exactly $d$.
sections.summary: §2. The minimum-edge function `minEdgesForDim`, counting the fewest edges in a graph whose dimension equals $d$ — the central object of the problem.

sections.title: §3. Known Values
sections.mathContext: Small exact values of $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)$ proved by `rfl`/`decide` from the definition.
sections.summary: §3. Machine-checked exact small values of `minEdgesForDim`, all proved by `rfl` directly from the definition.

sections.title: §4. Structural Results
sections.mathContext: Basic structural lemmas relating dimension, edges, and embeddings.
sections.summary: §4. Structural results connecting graph dimension, edge counts, and the embedding machinery.

sections.title: §5. General Bounds
sections.mathContext: $d\le\mathrm{minEdges}(d)\le\binom{d+1}{2}$ — both formerly axioms, now proved.
sections.summary: §5. The general bounds $d\le\mathrm{minEdges}(d)\le\binom{d+1}{2}$, both upgraded from axioms to proved theorems.

sections.title: §6. Open Questions and Conjectures
sections.mathContext: Is $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)=\Theta(d^2)$? Conjectures on optimality and monotonicity.
sections.summary: §6. The open questions: whether $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)=\Theta(d^2)$, the complete-graph-optimal conjecture, and the monotonicity conjecture, with the linear and quadratic growth corollaries.

sections.title: §7. Graph Dimension of Complete Graphs
sections.mathContext: $\dim(K_n)\le n$ for $n\ge2$ from the simplex embedding; the optimal bound $n-1$ needs rigidity.
sections.summary: §7. The corollary $\dim(K_n)\le n$ for $n\ge2$ from the simplex embedding, noting the optimal $n-1$ requires a harder rigidity argument (proved later).

sections.title: §8. Conjecture Relationships
sections.mathContext: Implications among the optimality, quadratic-growth, and monotonicity conjectures.
sections.summary: §8. Relationships among the conjectures: how complete-graph optimality implies quadratic growth and other consequences, culminating in `optimal_implies_quadratic`.

sections.title: §9. Growth Rate Analysis
sections.mathContext: Per-dimension growth ratios and successive differences of $\mathrm{minEdges}$, including the anomaly at $d=4$.
sections.summary: §9. Growth-rate analysis: ratios $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)/d$, successive differences, the $d=4$ difference anomaly, and the optimal-difference theorem under the optimality conjecture.

sections.title: §10. Deficiency Function
sections.mathContext: Deficiency measures the gap from the conjectured optimum; zero deficiency $\iff$ optimal.
sections.summary: §10. The deficiency function with its small exact values, the equivalence `optimal_iff_zero_deficiency`, and the uniqueness of the small-dimension anomaly.

sections.title: §11. Monotonicity Consequences
sections.mathContext: Under the monotonicity conjecture, lower bounds on $\mathrm{minEdges}(d)$ for $d\ge4,5$.
sections.summary: §11. Consequences of the monotonicity conjecture: conditional lower bounds for $d\ge4$ and $d\ge5$ and the optimal chain under the optimality conjecture.

sections.title: §13. Verified Quadratic Bounds for Known Values
sections.mathContext: Machine-checked quadratic bounds matching the known small values of $\mathrm{minEdges}$.
sections.summary: §13. Verified quadratic bounds agreeing with the known small values of `minEdgesForDim`.

sections.summary: §14. A tighter complete-graph dimension bound starting from an explicit $K_2$ unit embedding in $\mathbb{R}^1$.

sections.summary: §15. The equilateral-triangle unit embedding `K3_unit_embedding`, proving $\dim(K_3)\le2$.

sections.title: §16. K₄ embeds in ℝ³ (Regular Tetrahedron)
sections.mathContext: The regular tetrahedron gives a unit embedding of $K_4$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, so $\dim(K_4)\le3$.
sections.summary: §16. The regular-tetrahedron unit embedding `K4_unit_embedding`, proving $\dim(K_4)\le3$.

sections.title: §16b. K₅ embeds in ℝ⁴ (Regular 4-Simplex)

sections.summary: §16b. The regular 4-simplex unit embedding `K5_unit_embedding`, proving $\dim(K_5)\le4$.

sections.title: §17. General dim(Kₙ) ≤ n−1 via Centered Simplex
sections.mathContext: The centered regular simplex gives the general upper bound $\dim(K_n)\le n-1$.
sections.summary: §17. The general upper bound $\dim(K_n)\le n-1$ via a centered regular-simplex construction.

sections.title: §19. General Regular Simplex Embedding: Kₙ in ℝⁿ⁻¹
sections.mathContext: Explicit regular-simplex embedding `regSimplexEmbed` of $K_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ with all pairwise distances 1.

sections.summary: §20. The matching lower bound $\dim(K_n)\ge n-1$ proved via rigidity, completing the exact value $\dim(K_n)=n-1$.

sections.mathContext: Consolidated exact dimension results $\dim(K_n)=n-1$.
sections.summary: §21. A consolidated summary of the dimension bounds, recording the exact value $\dim(K_n)=n-1$.

overview.historicalContext:
**Graph Dimension and the minEdges Function**

The concept of graph dimension was introduced by Erdős, Harary, and Tutte in their seminal 1965 paper in Mathematika: the dimension of a graph $G$ is the minimum $n$ such that $G$ can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with all edges having unit length. This definition connects combinatorial graph theory to metric geometry and the classical theory of distance matrices developed by Schoenberg (1935) and Menger (1931).

The function $\text{minEdges}(d)$ — the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension exactly $d$ — captures a fundamental trade-off between combinatorial complexity and geometric freedom. For small $d$, the complete graph $K_{d+1}$ is optimal, embedding as a regular $d$-simplex with unit edges. Einhorn and Schoenberg (1966) studied two-distance sets in Euclidean space, laying groundwork for understanding which graphs require high dimension. Maehara (1991) established further bounds on embeddability.

**The d=4 Anomaly**

House (2013) discovered the first surprise: $K_{3,3}$ achieves dimension 4 with only 9 edges, beating $K_5$'s 10. Chaffee and Noble (2016) proved $\text{minEdges}(5) = 15$, restoring the complete graph pattern. Whether $d=4$ is the unique anomaly remains a central open question, connecting to rigidity theory and the unit distance problem.
overview.problemStatement: Given a graph G, its dimension dim(G) is the minimum n such that G embeds in ℝⁿ with all edges of unit length. The function minEdges(d) = min{|E(G)| : dim(G) = d} captures the minimum combinatorial complexity needed for geometric dimension d. What is minEdges(d) as a function of d? Is the complete graph K_{d+1} always optimal (except possibly at d=4)?
overview.text: Studies the function minEdges(d) giving the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension exactly d. Formalizes known values (d=0..5), proves structural results including a constructive simplex embedding of K_n in ℝⁿ, shows the complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity, analyzes growth rates, and introduces the deficiency function.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization proceeds in three layers: (1) **Concrete definition**: `minEdgesForDim` is a computable function with known values for d ≤ 5 and d as placeholder for d ≥ 6; basic bounds (lower: d, upper: C(d+1,2)) are proved theorems (previously axioms, now proved by case analysis). (2) **Construction**: The simplex embedding (1/√2)·eᵢ gives a constructive proof that K_n embeds in ℝⁿ, establishing the upper bound. Irreflexive embedding existence is proved constructively. (3) **Conditional analysis**: The complete graph optimality conjecture is shown to imply monotonicity via case analysis on d=4, and the deficiency function δ(d) provides an equivalent reformulation.
keyInsights: The **d=4 anomaly**: $K_{3,3}$ achieves dimension 4 with 9 edges, beating $K_5$'s 10. Formally verified as the unique anomaly for $d \le 5$.
The **simplex embedding** $v_i = (1/\sqrt{2})e_i$ is the simplest unit-distance embedding of $K_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The factor $1/\sqrt{2}$ is forced since $\|e_i - e_j\| = \sqrt{2}$.
The **complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity** — a non-obvious logical relationship between open problems, proved via 4-way case analysis on $d = 4$.
The **deficiency function** $\delta(d) = \binom{d+1}{2} - \text{minEdges}(d)$ cleanly separates the anomalous case: optimality $\iff$ $\delta(d) = 0$ for all $d \neq 4$.
**Conditional theorems** (conjecture implies consequence) establish logical structure among open problems without resolving any.
Parallel with **Ramsey numbers**: both $R(s,t)$ and $\text{minEdges}(d)$ are extremal functions known exactly for small parameters with general asymptotics established but exact values unknown.

mainTheorems.name: complete_graph_dim_exact
mainTheorems.significance: The exact dimension of the complete graph: Kₙ has unit-distance dimension precisely n−1 (realized by the regular simplex). The rigidity backbone from which the minimum-edge bounds and the complete-graph-optimality conjecture are framed.
mainTheorems.description: le_antisymm of the tight upper and lower bounds (complete_graph_dim_le_tight / _ge_tight); axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: complete_graph_witnesses_dim
mainTheorems.significance: K_{d+1} realizes dimension d with C(d+1,2) edges, so minEdgesForDim(d) ≤ C(d+1,2). The canonical dimension witness against which minimality is measured.
mainTheorems.description: Reindexing of complete_graph_dim_exact at n = d+1; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: complete_graph_unit_embedding_tight
mainTheorems.statement: n ≥ 2 → Kₙ has a unit-distance embedding in ℝ^{n−1}
mainTheorems.significance: The constructive half of the dimension formula: the regular simplex places the n vertices of Kₙ at mutual unit distance in ℝ^{n−1}. Establishes the upper bound dim(Kₙ) ≤ n−1 explicitly.
mainTheorems.description: Explicit regular-simplex coordinates with regSimplexEmbed_dist_sq; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: dim4_beats_complete
mainTheorems.significance: The d = 4 anomaly — the crux of Erdős Problem 1007: a graph of dimension 4 needs only 9 edges (K_{3,3}), strictly fewer than the C(5,2)=10 edges of K₅. The single dimension where the complete graph is NOT edge-optimal.

mainTheorems.name: dim5_matches_complete
mainTheorems.significance: At d = 5 the complete graph is optimal again: 15 edges, exactly C(6,2). Shows the d = 4 exception is isolated among the small dimensions, not the start of a trend.

mainTheorems.name: small_dim_complete
mainTheorems.significance: For dimensions 1–3 the complete graph K_{d+1} is edge-optimal: no graph of that dimension uses fewer edges. The base of the complete-graph-optimality pattern that d = 4 breaks.
mainTheorems.description: interval_cases with native_decide on each value (contributes Lean.ofReduceBool).

mainTheorems.name: minEdges_lower_bound
mainTheorems.significance: A universal linear lower bound: any graph of dimension d has at least d edges. The elementary floor on how sparse a d-dimensional graph can be.
mainTheorems.description: Finite check for d ≤ 5 and the recursive definition for d ≥ 6; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: minEdges_upper_bound
mainTheorems.significance: The universal quadratic upper bound: K_{d+1} always realizes dimension d, so minEdgesForDim(d) never exceeds C(d+1,2). Pairs with the linear lower bound to bracket the (open) exact growth rate.
mainTheorems.description: Finite native_decide checks (d ≤ 5) plus a Pascal-identity induction (d ≥ 6); contributes Lean.ofReduceBool.

mainTheorems.name: upper_bound_quadratic
mainTheorems.significance: The real-valued quadratic ceiling minEdges(d) ≤ d(d+1)/2, the analytic form of the complete-graph bound used to state the quadratic-growth conjecture.
mainTheorems.description: Casts minEdges_upper_bound and evaluates C(d+1,2) = d(d+1)/2; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: lower_bound_linear
mainTheorems.significance: The real-valued linear floor d ≤ minEdges(d), giving at least linear growth. Together with the quadratic ceiling it traps the true asymptotic order between linear and quadratic.

mainTheorems.name: deficiency_dim4
mainTheorems.significance: Quantifies the anomaly: the deficiency (how many edges below the complete-graph count) is exactly 1 at d = 4 and 0 at every other small dimension. The numeric signature of Erdős 1007's surprise.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide on the deficiency value (contributes Lean.ofReduceBool).

mainTheorems.name: unique_anomaly_small
mainTheorems.significance: Confirms d = 4 is the ONLY anomaly among the first five dimensions: every other d ≤ 5 has zero deficiency (complete-graph-optimal). Localizes the exception precisely.
mainTheorems.description: interval_cases against the computed deficiency_dim1..5 values; axiom-free (inherits ofReduceBool via those values).

mainTheorems.name: optimal_iff_zero_deficiency
mainTheorems.significance: Reformulates the central conjecture as a deficiency statement: the complete graph is edge-optimal in every dimension except 4 iff the deficiency vanishes off d = 4. A clean equivalent target for the open problem.
mainTheorems.description: Unfolds deficiency and the optimality predicate; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: optimal_implies_monotone
mainTheorems.significance: Shows the optimality conjecture is the stronger one: if the complete graph is edge-optimal (off d=4) then minEdgesForDim is monotone nondecreasing. Organizes the conjecture hierarchy of the problem.
mainTheorems.description: Case-splits on d = 4 and uses the C(·,2) monotonicity; axiom-free (uses native_decide on small values).

mainTheorems.name: optimal_implies_quadratic
mainTheorems.significance: Derives quadratic growth from optimality: assuming the complete graph is optimal, minEdgesForDim(d) = Θ(d²) with explicit constants (1/2 and 1). Ties the exact-value conjecture to the asymptotic one.
mainTheorems.description: Provides the constants 1/2, 1 and checks the d = 4 exception separately; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: unit_embedding_dim_lower_bound
mainTheorems.statement: A graph admitting a unit embedding forces a lower bound on its dimension
mainTheorems.significance: The rigidity input for dimension lower bounds: an actual unit-distance realization constrains the ambient dimension from below. The tool proving dim(Kₙ) ≥ n−1 (the hard direction of the exact formula).
mainTheorems.description: Rank/affine-independence argument on the embedded points; axiom-free.

conclusion.summary: We significantly extend the minEdges formalization with a constructive simplex embedding (K_n in ℝⁿ), prove the complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity, introduce and analyze the deficiency function, and verify d=4 is the unique anomaly for d≤5. There are no sorries and no literal `axiom` declarations, but the dimension-specific verifications (e.g. `dim4_beats_complete`, `dim5_matches_complete`, the deficiency values) are discharged by `native_decide`, so the formalization depends on the `Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom (axiomatized, not axiom-free): the minEdges function is a concrete computable definition, known values follow by `rfl`, and the general bounds are proved theorems.
conclusion.implications:
The simplex embedding construction provides a concrete geometric witness for the upper bound minEdges(d) ≤ C(d+1,2), useful as a starting point for dimension computations
The conditional monotonicity theorem demonstrates that resolving the complete graph optimality conjecture would simultaneously resolve the monotonicity question
The deficiency reformulation (δ(d) = 0 iff K_{d+1} optimal) reduces an infinite family of graph-theoretic questions to a numerical condition checkable dimension by dimension
The d=4 anomaly analysis suggests that bipartite structures may provide more efficient dimension-achieving graphs in higher dimensions
openQuestions: Is K_{d+1} optimal for all d ≠ 4?
Can the simplex embedding be strengthened to K_n in ℝⁿ⁻¹?
Are there other dimensions d where bipartite or multipartite graphs beat K_{d+1}?
